stories.headline: OpenAI acquires Python toolmaker Astral to strengthen Codex, which now has 2M+ weekly active users

key_facts.fact: OpenAI announced on March 19 it will acquire Astral, the startup behind uv (package manager), Ruff (linter/formatter), and ty (type checker) — open-source Python tools with hundreds of millions of monthly downloads. The Astral team will join the Codex group.
key_facts.excerpt: Today we're announcing that OpenAI will acquire Astral, bringing powerful open source developer tools into our Codex ecosystem.

key_facts.fact: Codex has over 2 million weekly active users, with 3x user growth and 5x usage increase since the start of the year. OpenAI's goal is to move beyond code generation toward systems that participate in the full development workflow.
key_facts.excerpt: Codex has already seen 3x user growth and 5x usage increase since the start of the year, and has over 2 million weekly active users.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI said it will continue supporting Astral's open-source tools after the deal closes. Founder Charlie Marsh said: 'If our goal is to make programming more productive, then building at the frontier of AI and software feels like the highest-leverage thing we can do.'
key_facts.excerpt: Open source is at the heart of that impact and the heart of that story; it sits at the center of everything we do. In line with our philosophy and OpenAI's own announcement, OpenAI will continue supporting our open source tools after the deal closes.

key_facts.fact: The acquisition is a direct competitive response to Anthropic's Claude Code, which has been 'steadily pulling professional developers away,' according to the Times of India. Codex Lead Thibault Sottiaux said the goal is to make Codex 'the agent most capable of working across the entire software developer lifecycle.'
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic's Claude Code has been steadily pulling professional developers away, and OpenAI needs Codex to be more than a code generator to fight back.

key_facts.fact: uv alone was downloaded more than 126 million times last month according to PyPI Stats. Simon Willison noted the Astral team includes BurntSushi (creator of Rust regex, ripgrep, jiff), calling the talent dimension 'may be worth the price of acquisition.'
key_facts.excerpt: According to PyPI Stats uv was downloaded more than 126 million times last month! Since its release in February 2024—just two years ago—it's become one of the most popular tools for running Python code.

stories.headline: OpenAI merging ChatGPT, Codex, and Atlas browser into one desktop 'superapp' amid Anthropic pressure

key_facts.fact: OpenAI is consolidating its ChatGPT app, Codex coding platform, and Atlas AI browser into a single desktop 'superapp,' according to a Wall Street Journal report on March 19-20. The move aims to eliminate product fragmentation and focus resources on core offerings.
key_facts.excerpt: The Wall Street Journal has new details on OpenAI's plan to roll its various products into a single desktop app. The company wants to combine ChatGPT, the Codex coding platform, and its Atlas browser into what it's calling a 'superapp.'

key_facts.fact: Fidji Simo, OpenAI's CEO of Applications, wrote in an internal memo that spreading the company across too many apps had 'been slowing us down and making it harder to hit the quality bar we want.' Sam Altman and Head of Research Mark Chen are evaluating which initiatives to scale back.
key_facts.excerpt: CEO of Applications Fidji Simo laid out the new direction in a company-wide meeting, with Sam Altman and Head of Research Mark Chen evaluating which initiatives to scale back.

key_facts.fact: President Greg Brockman is temporarily leading the overhaul. Simo said publicly: 'When new bets start to work, like we're seeing now with Codex, it's very important to double down on them and avoid distractions.'
key_facts.excerpt: Head of Applications Fidji Simo and President Greg Brockman are spearheading the merger to cut the clutter and sharpen the ecosystem's focus.

key_facts.fact: The pivot is a direct response to Anthropic's growing enterprise dominance. The Decoder noted that 'Anthropic's desktop app already combines chat, the productivity application Cowork, and Claude Code in a single app,' positioning the OpenAI superapp as a catch-up move.
key_facts.excerpt: The strategic pivot comes as a direct response to Anthropic's growing dominance in the enterprise AI market, where its Claude Code and Cowork products have made it the go-to provider for businesses.

key_facts.fact: The mobile ChatGPT app will remain standalone. The superapp will emphasize 'agentic' AI capabilities that can autonomously handle complex tasks for developers and enterprise users.
key_facts.excerpt: The mobile version of ChatGPT is unaffected by these changes and will continue to be available as a standalone application — meaning the focus on end consumers on smartphones remains intact.

stories.headline: Google begins beta-testing native Gemini Mac app with 'Desktop Intelligence' to rival ChatGPT and Claude

key_facts.fact: Google started privately sharing an early version of a dedicated Gemini AI app for Mac with beta testers this week, according to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman on March 19. The app is designed to compete with OpenAI's ChatGPT and Anthropic's Claude desktop apps.
key_facts.excerpt: Google is developing a native Gemini app for the Mac, reports Bloomberg. Right now, Mac users who want to use Google's Gemini AI have to use a web browser, but that will change with a dedicated Mac app.

key_facts.fact: The app includes a 'Desktop Intelligence' feature that allows Gemini to read the user's screen and pull content directly from other Mac apps, mirroring functionality available in tools like Claude Cowork. Google told testers the current version has only 'critical features.'
key_facts.excerpt: When you enable apps for Desktop Intelligence you are enabling Gemini to see what you see (such as screen context) and pull content directly from these apps to improve and personalize your experience only when Gemini is in use.

key_facts.fact: Testers are evaluating content generation tools for images, tables and charts, video, and music, plus web search, document analysis, mathematical problem-solving, and conversation history. The interface looks similar to the existing iPhone and iPad Gemini apps.
key_facts.excerpt: Google is asking users to test content generation tools for images, tables and charts, video, music, and more, plus provide feedback on mathematical questions and information analysis.

key_facts.fact: There is no confirmed release date. The move fills a significant gap for Google — Mac users currently must use a web browser for Gemini, while competitors Anthropic and OpenAI both offer native Mac apps.
key_facts.excerpt: It's a glaring hole in accessibility for Gemini, with macOS users currently being required to access the platform via the web. Meanwhile, companies like Anthropic and OpenAI offer dedicated Mac apps for Claude and ChatGPT, respectively.

stories.headline: Deeptune raises $43M Series A led by a16z to build 'training gyms' for AI agents using reinforcement learning

key_facts.fact: Deeptune raised a $43 million Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz, announced March 19. The startup builds high-fidelity reinforcement learning environments that simulate professional workflows across enterprise software like Slack, Salesforce, and ticketing systems.
key_facts.excerpt: AI startup Deeptune has raised a $43 million Series A to build what it calls 'training gyms' for AI agents, Fortune has learned exclusively. Andreessen Horowitz led the round.

key_facts.fact: CEO Tim Lupo compared today's AI agents to 'pilots who have only ever read books or watched tutorials' and said Deeptune builds 'essentially the flight simulators for AI doing work across the economy.' The ~20-person team is based in New York.
key_facts.excerpt: We essentially build simulations of digital work that look like the workspace of an accountant or a lawyer or a software engineer.

key_facts.fact: Other investors include 776, Abstract Ventures, and Inspired Capital. Angel investors include OpenAI researcher Noam Brown, Mercor CEO Brendan Foody, and Applied Compute CEO Yash Patil. The team includes engineers from Anthropic, Scale AI, Palantir, and Retool.
key_facts.excerpt: Andreessen Horowitz led the round, joined by 776, Abstract Ventures, and Inspired Capital, with angels including OpenAI researcher Noam Brown, Mercor CEO Brendan Foody, and Applied Compute CEO Yash Patil.

key_facts.fact: The round addresses the growing industry concern about 'data exhaustion' — the idea that training agents on static web data is insufficient and interactive RL environments are needed. The global reinforcement learning market is projected to grow from $11.6 billion to over $90 billion by 2034.
key_facts.excerpt: Artificial intelligence startup Deeptune Inc. said today it's going to solve the industry's 'data exhaustion' crisis after raising $43 million in an early-stage funding.

stories.headline: Autoscience raises $14M to build autonomous AI research lab that invents and deploys ML models without humans

key_facts.fact: Autoscience announced $14M in seed funding on March 18-19 to build an autonomous AI laboratory where non-human AI scientists and engineers invent, validate, and deploy specialized machine learning models. General Catalyst led the round, with Toyota Ventures, Perplexity Fund, MaC Ventures, and S32 participating.
key_facts.excerpt: Artificial intelligence startup Autoscience Institute has launched with $14 million in seed funding to automate research into new machine learning models.

key_facts.fact: CEO Eliot Cowan said the objective is to 'compress a decade of machine learning research into months.' The company argues that with 2,000+ ML papers published weekly, no human team can evaluate and implement every breakthrough while advancing original hypotheses.
key_facts.excerpt: We've reached a point where human intuition is no longer enough to navigate the complexity of algorithmic discovery.

key_facts.fact: Autoscience's AI agent 'Carl' became the first AI system to produce a peer-reviewed scientific paper, accepted to the ICLR 2025 workshop track. The paper, 'Investigating Alignment Signals in Initial Token Representations,' required only minor human edits for citations and formatting.
key_facts.excerpt: Autoscience first gained recognition when its autonomous lab became the first AI system to produce a peer-reviewed scientific research paper.

key_facts.fact: The founding team includes former GoogleX, MIT, and Harvard researchers. First deployments target high-stakes financial applications, manufacturing, and fraud detection, enabling companies to benefit from AI research output without needing a full research division.
key_facts.excerpt: Backed by General Catalyst and Perplexity Fund, the former GoogleX, MIT, and Harvard team is building an AI lab where new models are invented autonomously using AI systems.

stories.headline: Snowflake launches Project SnowWork, an agentic AI platform that autonomously executes enterprise workflows

key_facts.fact: Snowflake announced the research preview of Project SnowWork on March 19, an autonomous enterprise AI platform where business users describe tasks in natural language and AI agents plan and execute multi-step workflows end-to-end across governed Snowflake data.
key_facts.excerpt: Snowflake announced the research preview of Project SnowWork, a new autonomous enterprise AI platform designed to help business users massively accelerate workflows.

key_facts.fact: CEO Sridhar Ramaswamy said: 'We are entering the era of the agentic enterprise, ushering in a fundamentally new way to work. This shift is about much more than technology, it's about unlocking new levels of productivity and efficiency by embedding intelligence directly into the operating fabric of the enterprise.'
key_facts.excerpt: We are entering the era of the agentic enterprise, ushering in a fundamentally new way to work.

key_facts.fact: SnowWork includes pre-built, persona-specific AI 'profiles' for finance, sales, marketing, and operations roles. Use cases include board-ready forecast decks, churn risk spreadsheets, and supply chain bottleneck analysis — all generated autonomously from conversational prompts.
key_facts.excerpt: Snowflake says SnowWork (currently in research preview) is a key step toward its vision of an AI-driven enterprise, where governed data powers automated decisions and workflows across the organization.

key_facts.fact: Unlike general-purpose AI agents, SnowWork runs on a company's own governed data with role-based access controls, masking policies, and audit logging built in. It represents Snowflake's push beyond analytics into autonomous execution.
key_facts.excerpt: SnowWork is positioned as an extension of Snowflake's AI Data Cloud, and is meant for employees across functions such as finance, sales, and operations.

stories.headline: OpenAI shifts strategy from consumer products toward enterprise and coding tools amid Anthropic's surge

key_facts.fact: Ramp data published March 18 shows Anthropic now captures over 73% of all spending among companies buying AI tools for the first time, up from a 50/50 split with OpenAI just 10 weeks earlier. In early December it was 60/40 in OpenAI's favor.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic is now capturing over 73% of all spending among companies buying AI tools for the first time, according to customer data from Ramp.

key_facts.fact: The Wall Street Journal reported on March 19 that OpenAI leaders are looking at things to deprioritize, with Simo telling employees last week they needed to avoid being 'distracted by side quests.' The company is shifting from consumer bets like Sora and hardware toward enterprise and coding.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI is shifting its strategy away from spreading resources across multiple product lines, instead narrowing its focus to coding tools and enterprise customers.

key_facts.fact: Ramp data showed Anthropic's business subscriptions grew 4.9% month over month in February, while OpenAI's subscription share fell during the same period. Multiple Fortune 500 executives told Axios they don't want to pick just one model yet.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic has been killing it in the business market, success that appears to be at least partially attributable to pushback against the Pentagon. The maker of the Claude family of models saw business software subscriptions grow 4.9 percent month over month in February.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI says it is on pace to generate $25 billion in revenue this year, versus Anthropic's $19 billion. But Anthropic's strength in AI coding tools — particularly Claude Code — is a 'key advantage' according to Mizuho analyst Jordan Klein, who called the shift 'super bullish' for Amazon, which runs most of Anthropic's inference.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI says it's on pace to generate $25 billion in revenue this year, versus Anthropic's $19 billion. But Anthropic appears to be accelerating faster.

stories.headline: Super Micro co-founder charged with smuggling $2.5B in Nvidia AI chips to China

key_facts.fact: The U.S. Attorney's Office for the Southern District of New York unsealed an indictment on March 19 charging Yih-Shyan 'Wally' Liaw (71, co-founder and SVP of Super Micro Computer), Ruei-Tsang 'Steven' Chang (53, sales manager in Super Micro's Taiwan office), and Ting-Wei 'Willy' Sun (44, a contractor) with conspiring to violate the Export Control Reform Act, smuggling goods, and conspiracy to defraud the US.
key_facts.excerpt: The U.S. Attorney's Office for the Southern District of New York has charged associates of an unidentified U.S. server maker with illegally diverting billions of dollars in Nvidia-powered servers to China.

key_facts.fact: The defendants allegedly diverted approximately $2.5 billion in high-performance servers containing Nvidia B200 'Blackwell' GPUs to a middleman company in Southeast Asia that forwarded the hardware to China, using unmarked boxes, staged dummy non-working servers in Southeast Asian warehouses to fool auditors, and falsified documentation.
key_facts.excerpt: Servers shipped in unmarked boxes to conceal their contents. Non-working units were placed in Southeast Asian warehouses to fool auditors. The group prepared phony communications to ensure internal approval of the shipments.

key_facts.fact: Liaw was arrested in California and released on bail; Sun is held awaiting a detention hearing; Chang remains at large. Liaw controls $464 million worth of Super Micro shares. The charges carry maximum sentences of 20 years (export control conspiracy), 5 years (smuggling conspiracy), and 5 years (fraud conspiracy).
key_facts.excerpt: Liaw, who co-founded Super Micro Computer and served on its board of directors, was arrested Thursday in California and released on bail. Sun, a contractor, is held awaiting a detention hearing. Chang, who worked in the Taiwan office of Super Micro, remains at large.

key_facts.fact: Super Micro shares dropped 12% in extended trading. The company placed Liaw and Chang on administrative leave, terminated Sun, and stated the alleged conduct 'is a contravention of the Company's policies and compliance controls.' Super Micro accounts for roughly 9% of Nvidia's revenue.
key_facts.excerpt: Shares of Super Micro fell about 12% in extended trading. Super Micro said one of the defendants was a co-founder and executive, another was a manager, and the third was a contractor.

stories.headline: Samsung plans record $73B investment in 2026 to retake AI chip lead from SK Hynix

key_facts.excerpt: Samsung Electronics said on Thursday that it plans to invest more than 110 trillion won ($73.24 billion) this year in research and development and facilities in a bid to lead the semiconductor industry in artificial intelligence.

key_facts.fact: The record outlay surpasses TSMC's roughly $50 billion capex for 2026 and is aimed at retaking the lead in AI chips from SK Hynix, which has become the dominant provider of high-bandwidth memory to Nvidia.
key_facts.excerpt: Korea's largest company is hiking investment 22% in 2026 to try and retake the lead in AI chips from SK Hynix Inc., which has become the dominant provider of high-bandwidth memory to Nvidia Corp. The total outlay surpasses the roughly $50 billion that Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. is setting aside for capex this year.

key_facts.fact: Samsung's filing also disclosed plans to pursue meaningful M&A in areas including robots, medical technology, auto electronics, and air-conditioning solutions, and to pay 9.8 trillion won in regular dividends for 2026.

stories.headline: Uber invests up to $1.25B in Rivian for fleet of 50,000 R2 robotaxis across 25 cities

key_facts.fact: Uber and Rivian announced on March 19 a deal for Uber to invest up to $1.25 billion in Rivian through 2031, with an initial $300 million committed upon signing subject to regulatory approval, in exchange for purchasing 10,000 fully autonomous Rivian R2 robotaxis with an option for up to 40,000 more beginning in 2030.
key_facts.excerpt: Uber Technologies plans to invest up to $1.25 billion in electric vehicle maker Rivian Automotive as part of a deal to deploy up to 50,000 robotaxis in several countries through 2031.

key_facts.fact: Commercial service is planned to begin in San Francisco and Miami in 2028, expanding to 25 cities across the US, Canada, and Europe by 2031. Vehicles will be available exclusively through the Uber platform.
key_facts.excerpt: Commercial service is planned to begin in San Francisco and Miami in 2028 and expand to 25 cities across the US, Canada, and Europe by 2031. The vehicles will be available exclusively through the Uber platform.

key_facts.fact: Rivian's R2 autonomy platform is built on its in-house RAP1 inference chip and features 11 cameras, 5 radars, and 1 LiDAR unit. CEO RJ Scaringe said the deal reflects Rivian's vertically integrated approach to autonomy, from silicon to software.
key_facts.excerpt: The scale of Rivian's growing data flywheel coupled with RAP1, our state of the art in-house inference platform, and our multi-modal perception platform make us incredibly excited for the rapid advancement of Rivian autonomy over the next couple of years.

key_facts.fact: The deal marks a major shift for Uber, which sold its self-driving unit ATG after a fatal crash in 2018 and years of heavy losses, then pivoted to partnerships with existing operators like Waymo. Rivian shares rose as much as 10% on the news before closing 3% higher; Uber fell 1%.
key_facts.excerpt: Shares of Rivian jumped in premarket trading Thursday, rising roughly 10% before paring back those gains, closing the day 3% higher, while Uber's stock fell 1%.

stories.headline: Blue Origin files FCC plan for 51,600 orbital data center satellites under 'Project Sunrise'

key_facts.fact: Blue Origin filed with the FCC on March 19 to deploy up to 51,600 data center satellites under 'Project Sunrise,' arguing that 'insatiable demand for AI workloads' means orbiting servers represent 'a complement to terrestrial infrastructure by introducing a new compute tier that operates independently of Earth-based constraints.'
key_facts.excerpt: A Thursday filing argues that the US Federal Communications Commission should approve Blue Origin's plans because 'insatiable demand for AI workloads' means orbiting servers represent 'a complement to terrestrial infrastructure by introducing a new compute tier that operates independently of Earth-based constraints.'

key_facts.fact: The planned satellites would orbit at altitudes of 500-1,800 km in sun-synchronous orbits with inclinations between 97-104 degrees, connected by optical inter-satellite links. The system depends on Blue Origin's TeraWave broadband service (5,000+ satellites, first launch targeted before end of 2027) for Earth connectivity.
key_facts.excerpt: Space-based datacenters can help break this bottleneck. The built-in efficiencies of solar-powered satellites, always-on solar energy, lack of land or displacement costs, and nonexistent grid infrastructure disparities, fundamentally lower the marginal cost of compute capacity compared to terrestrial alternatives.

key_facts.fact: The filing follows SpaceX's January 2026 application for up to 1 million orbital data center satellites, and Starcloud's March filing for 88,000 satellites, signaling an intensifying race for orbital compute. Amazon's satellite division previously petitioned the FCC to block SpaceX's proposal.
key_facts.excerpt: The Starcloud proposal is far smaller than SpaceX's proposal, filed with the FCC at the end of January, to develop a constellation of up to one million orbital data center satellites.

key_facts.fact: Industry experts remain skeptical, noting the technology for orbiting data centers doesn't yet exist and will likely be unreliable. Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket has only flown twice, and no TeraWave satellites are operational.
key_facts.excerpt: Those claims are hotly contested on grounds that the technology for orbiting datacenters doesn't exist and will likely be unreliable and therefore impractical.

stories.headline: K2 Space readies 2-ton Gravitas satellite for launch, targeting orbital data centers

key_facts.fact: K2 Space, founded by former SpaceX engineers Karan and Neel Kunjur in 2022, has packed its 2-metric-ton Gravitas satellite into a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket for launch as soon as late March 2026, demonstrating technology required to build data centers in orbit.
key_facts.excerpt: K2 Space, founded by brothers and former SpaceX engineers Karan and Neel Kunjur in 2022, has packed its satellite Gravitas into a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket expected to launch as soon as the end of this month.

key_facts.fact: Gravitas generates 20 kW of power with a 40-meter solar wingspan, placing it among the highest-powered spacecraft ever built. It will carry 12 payloads from the Department of Defense and commercial customers, backed by a $60 million U.S. Space Force contract.
key_facts.excerpt: Mission carries 12 payloads from Department of Defense and commercial customers, backed by $60 million U.S. Space Force contract. K2 Space's Gravitas mission satellite, weighing 2 metric tons with a 40-meter solar wingspan, will generate 20 kW of power.

key_facts.fact: The mission will test a 20 kW Hall-effect thruster to raise orbit from low Earth orbit (LEO) to medium Earth orbit (MEO). K2 Space has raised $250 million at a $3 billion valuation, with $72 million in prior funding.

stories.headline: NASA rolls Artemis II moon rocket to launch pad ahead of April 1 crewed lunar mission

key_facts.fact: NASA's Artemis II SLS rocket and Orion spacecraft began rolling to Launch Pad 39B at Kennedy Space Center at 12:20 a.m. EDT on March 20, after high winds delayed the planned March 19 evening rollout. The 4-mile trek takes up to 12 hours via crawler-transporter 2.
key_facts.excerpt: NASA's Artemis II SLS (Space Launch System) rocket and Orion spacecraft slated to send four astronauts around the Moon began rolling to Launch Pad 39B at 12:20 a.m. EDT on Friday, March 20.

key_facts.fact: The rollout follows repairs inside the Vehicle Assembly Building after a successful wet dress rehearsal on February 21 revealed a helium flow issue with the rocket's upper stage. Engineers also refreshed flight termination system batteries and other systems.
key_facts.excerpt: Following a successful wet dress rehearsal on Feb. 21, teams identified an issue preventing helium from flowing to the rocket's upper stage, prompting a return to the Vehicle Assembly Building where the issue was repaired.

key_facts.fact: Artemis II will send four astronauts — NASA's Victor Glover, Reid Wiseman, and Christina Koch, and the Canadian Space Agency's Jeremy Hansen — around the Moon, targeting an April 1 launch. The crew entered quarantine on March 19.

stories.headline: Iran hits Kuwait's largest refinery, escalates strikes across Gulf energy infrastructure

key_facts.fact: Iran launched drone strikes on Kuwait's Mina al-Ahmadi refinery, the country's largest, which processes approximately 730,000 barrels of oil per day. Fires broke out across multiple units on March 20 as Kuwaitis marked Eid al-Fitr, marking the second consecutive day the facility was targeted.
key_facts.excerpt: Fires broke out across multiple units at the Mina al-Ahmadi refinery, which processes about 730,000 barrels of oil per day, early on Friday morning, as Kuwaitis marked Eid al-Fitr.

key_facts.fact: Qatar's energy minister said the country's LNG export capacity will be reduced by 17% over the next five years due to Iranian attacks on the Ras Laffan facility, representing an estimated $20 billion annual revenue impact and a 3-to-5-year repair timeline.
key_facts.excerpt: Qatar's energy minister says its liquefied natural gas export capacity will be reduced by 17% over the next five years as a result of an Iranian attack on the Ras Laffan facility.

key_facts.fact: An Iranian drone struck a Saudi Aramco refinery in Yanbu on the Red Sea, a joint venture with ExxonMobil, while the UAE, Bahrain, Kuwait, and Saudi Arabia all reported additional missile or drone attacks on March 19-20.
key_facts.excerpt: An Iranian drone struck a Saudi Aramco refinery in Yanbu, on the Red Sea, on Thursday, according to the Saudi Ministry of Defense.

key_facts.excerpt: Israel pounded Tehran with airstrikes Friday as Iranians marked Nowruz, or the Persian New Year. The attacks came a day after Israel pledged to refrain from more strikes on a key Iranian gas field.

key_facts.fact: Heavy explosions shook Dubai early on March 20 as the conflict risked drawing Iran's Arab neighbors directly into the war, with the UAE, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, and Bahrain all reporting missile or drone attacks on their territory.

stories.headline: Trump administration weighs deploying thousands of US troops as Iran war enters new phase

key_facts.fact: The Trump administration is considering deploying thousands of additional US troops to reinforce operations in the Middle East as the Iran war enters its third week, according to a US official and three people familiar with the matter cited by Reuters.
key_facts.excerpt: President Donald Trump's administration is considering deploying thousands of U.S. troops to reinforce its operation in the Middle East, as the U.S. military prepares for possible next steps in its campaign against Iran.

key_facts.fact: Options under consideration include securing safe passage for oil tankers through the Strait of Hormuz using air and naval forces, as well as deploying ground forces to Iran's shoreline and potentially to Iran's Kharg Island, the hub for most of Iran's oil exports.
key_facts.excerpt: Those options include securing safe passage for oil tankers through the Strait of Hormuz. But securing the Strait could also mean deploying U.S. troops to Iran's shoreline. The Trump administration has also discussed options to send ground forces to Iran's Kharg Island.

key_facts.fact: Trump told reporters on March 19 that he is 'not putting troops anywhere,' contradicting the internal deliberations reported by Reuters. Deployment of ground forces could anger parts of Trump's political base opposed to new Middle East entanglements.
key_facts.excerpt: President Donald Trump told reporters he's 'not putting troops anywhere' after being asked about the possibility of deploying additional troops.

key_facts.fact: The Pentagon is seeking an additional $200 billion for Iran war operations. The US military has been primarily conducting air and naval operations since the war began on February 28.
key_facts.excerpt: The Pentagon is seeking an additional $200 billion for Iran war operations.

stories.headline: Kremlin confirms Ukraine peace talks on 'situational pause' as Iran war diverts US attention

key_facts.fact: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov confirmed on March 19 that talks between Washington, Moscow, and Kyiv on ending the war in Ukraine are on a 'situational pause, for obvious reasons' following the start of the Iran war.
key_facts.excerpt: 'The three-way group is on hold,' Dmitry Peskov, Russian President Vladimir Putin's spokesperson, told the Izvestia newspaper Thursday.

key_facts.fact: The last trilateral meeting was in February in Geneva. A new round of talks scheduled for March 5 in Abu Dhabi was postponed indefinitely, days after the US and Israel launched the attack on Iran on February 28.
key_facts.excerpt: The last time the three parties met was in February in Geneva. A new round of talks scheduled for March 5 in Abu Dhabi was postponed indefinitely, days after the U.S. and Israel launched an attack on Iran.

key_facts.fact: Ukrainian President Zelenskyy told the BBC he had a 'very bad feeling' about the Iran war's effect on Ukraine negotiations, saying talks were 'constantly being postponed.' However, he also said new discussions were expected over the weekend and that Washington had sent signals it was ready to continue.
key_facts.excerpt: Zelenskyy said he had a 'very bad feeling' about the effect of the events in Iran on the war in Ukraine. Negotiations, he said, were 'constantly being postponed. There is one reason: [the] war in Iran.'

key_facts.fact: Russia's Izvestia reported the Kremlin believes the Iran war could push Kyiv towards compromise. Economic cooperation talks between Moscow and Washington, led by envoy Kirill Dmitriev who has discussed joint projects worth up to $14 trillion, will continue alongside prisoner swap negotiations.
key_facts.excerpt: The Kremlin's envoy Kirill Dmitriev has previously suggested the two sides were eyeing joint projects worth up to $14 trillion. Russia has also long been lobbying for the United States to lift economic sanctions.

stories.headline: Super Micro co-founder charged with smuggling $2.5B in Nvidia AI chips to China

key_facts.fact: Super Micro Computer co-founder Yih-Shyan 'Wally' Liaw and two others were charged on March 19 with conspiring to divert $2.5 billion worth of servers containing Nvidia AI chips to China in violation of US export control laws, according to an indictment unsealed in Manhattan federal court.
key_facts.excerpt: The co-founder of Super Micro Computer and two others were charged with diverting $2.5 billion worth of servers with Nvidia's artificial intelligence chips to China, in violation of US laws barring exports to that country without a license.

key_facts.fact: The scheme involved sending US-made servers through Taiwan to other countries in Southeast Asia, where they were swapped into unmarked boxes and sent onward to China. Defendants used fabricated documents and staged bogus equipment to pass audit inventories.
key_facts.excerpt: A complex scheme to send US-made servers through Taiwan to other countries in Southeast Asia, where they were swapped into unmarked boxes and sent on to China.

key_facts.fact: Liaw, who co-founded Super Micro in 1993 and controls $464 million worth of company shares, was arrested in California and released on bail. Co-defendant Ruei-Tsang 'Steven' Chang, who worked in Super Micro's Taiwan office, remains at large. Ting-Wei 'Willy' Sun, a contractor, is detained.
key_facts.excerpt: Liaw, who co-founded Super Micro Computer and served on its board of directors, was arrested Thursday in California and released on bail. Chang remains at large. Sun is held awaiting a detention hearing.

key_facts.fact: Super Micro shares fell approximately 12% in extended trading. The company placed Liaw and Chang on administrative leave, terminated its relationship with Sun, and said it maintains a 'robust compliance program.' Super Micro itself was not named as a defendant.
key_facts.excerpt: Super Micro Computer is not named in the indictment. The company released a statement saying it has placed Liaw and Chang on administrative leave and terminated its relationship with Sun.

stories.headline: HSBC weighs cutting 20,000 jobs over 3-5 years as CEO bets on AI to reshape operations

key_facts.fact: HSBC is weighing deep job cuts that could ultimately impact around 20,000 roles, or about 10% of its 208,720 full-time equivalent workforce, as part of a multi-year AI-driven restructuring under CEO Georges Elhedery, according to Bloomberg News.
key_facts.excerpt: HSBC Holdings Plc is weighing deep job cuts over the coming years as Chief Executive Officer Georges Elhedery bets on AI to shrink its middle and back offices. The changes could ultimately impact around 20,000 roles — or about 10% of its total workforce.

key_facts.fact: Non-client-facing roles in global service centers are expected to be most impacted. The plan spans three to five years and could include not replacing departing staff as well as cuts tied to business exits or sales. The assessment is at an early stage with no final decisions made.
key_facts.excerpt: Non-client facing roles in global service centers are among those expected to be most impacted although the assessment is at an early stage.

key_facts.fact: CFO Pam Kaur said HSBC aims to deploy AI across customer service, transaction monitoring, and compliance processes including know-your-customer protocols. Hong Kong-listed HSBC shares fell 2.2% following the report.
key_facts.excerpt: CFO Pam Kaur said the bank aims to deploy AI across key areas such as customer service, transaction monitoring, and compliance processes including know-your-customer protocols.

key_facts.fact: Analysts predict global banks could eliminate up to 200,000 roles in coming years as digital adoption accelerates, with an average 3% workforce reduction across the industry. HSBC's plan would be among the largest AI-driven layoffs in the banking sector.
key_facts.excerpt: Global banks could eliminate up to 200,000 roles in coming years as digital adoption accelerates, with analysts predicting an average 3% workforce reduction across the industry.

stories.headline: FDA approves Wegovy HD (7.2mg), delivering ~21% weight loss in fastest GLP-1 approval yet

key_facts.fact: The FDA approved Wegovy HD (semaglutide 7.2mg injection) on March 19 for weight loss in adults with obesity, marking the fourth approval under the Commissioner's National Priority Voucher program. The decision came just 54 days after filing, a record pace.
key_facts.excerpt: The decision was granted just 54 days after filing and represented the fourth approval under the Commissioner's National Priority Voucher (CNPV) pilot program.

key_facts.fact: In the STEP UP trial, Wegovy HD achieved average weight loss of approximately 20.7% at 72 weeks in adults with obesity, compared to ~15% for the standard 2.4mg dose. About one in three participants achieved 25% or greater weight loss.
key_facts.excerpt: In the STEP UP trial, about one in three trial participants taking Wegovy HD achieved 25% weight loss or higher. Average weight loss of ~21% at 72 weeks in adults with obesity.

key_facts.fact: FDA Commissioner Martin Makary said: 'The new FDA is moving with unprecedented efficiency on products that advance national priorities. Today's approval is another demonstration of what the FDA can accomplish when we try bold new things.'
key_facts.excerpt: 'The new FDA is moving with unprecedented efficiency on products that advance national priorities. Today's approval is another demonstration of what the FDA can accomplish when we try bold new things.'

key_facts.fact: Novo Nordisk expects to launch the 7.2mg dose in April. The higher dose positions Wegovy to better compete with Eli Lilly's Zepbound, which has proven more effective at promoting weight loss than standard Wegovy. Dysesthesia (altered skin sensation) occurred more frequently at the higher dose (22.9%).
key_facts.excerpt: Dysesthesia occurred markedly more often at 7.2 mg (22.9%); symptoms typically resolved, and the FDA is investigating this signal.

stories.headline: Eli Lilly's triple-agonist retatrutide clears first Phase 3 trial with up to 17% weight loss

key_facts.fact: Eli Lilly announced positive topline results from TRANSCEND-T2D-1, the first Phase 3 trial of retatrutide, a first-in-class GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple hormone receptor agonist, in 537 patients with Type 2 diabetes over 40 weeks.
key_facts.excerpt: Eli Lilly and Company today announced positive topline results from TRANSCEND-T2D-1, a Phase 3 clinical trial evaluating the efficacy and safety of retatrutide, an investigational first-in-class GIP, GLP-1 and glucagon triple hormone receptor agonist.

key_facts.fact: Retatrutide lowered A1C by an average of 1.7% to 2.0% across doses at 40 weeks (vs. 0.8% placebo). At the 12mg dose, patients lost an average 16.8% of body weight (36.6 lbs), with no weight loss plateau observed through 40 weeks.
key_facts.excerpt: Retatrutide lowered A1C by an average of 1.7% to 2.0% across doses at 40 weeks. Participants taking retatrutide 12 mg lost an average of 36.6 lbs (16.8%). No weight loss plateau was observed.

key_facts.fact: The most common adverse events were gastrointestinal: nausea (16-27% vs. 4% placebo), diarrhea (19-26% vs. 5% placebo), and vomiting (15-18% vs. 2% placebo), primarily during dose escalation. Dysesthesia occurred in 2-5% of patients.
key_facts.excerpt: Most common adverse events included nausea (16.4%-26.5% vs. 3.7% placebo), diarrhea (18.7%-26.3% vs. 4.5% placebo), and vomiting (15.0%-17.6% vs. 2.2% placebo).

key_facts.fact: Detailed results will be presented at the American Diabetes Association Scientific Sessions in June. Additional Phase 3 results are expected over the next year. Lilly is betting on retatrutide as the next pillar of its obesity portfolio after Zepbound and upcoming oral drug orforglipron.
key_facts.excerpt: Detailed results will be presented at the American Diabetes Association Scientific Sessions in June; additional Phase 3 results expected over the next year.

stories.headline: J&J's icotrokinra becomes first targeted oral treatment for moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis

key_facts.fact: The FDA approved Johnson & Johnson's ICOTYDE (icotrokinra), the first and only oral peptide targeting the IL-23 receptor, for treatment of moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis in adults and pediatric patients aged 12+ weighing at least 40 kg.
key_facts.excerpt: Johnson & Johnson announced today that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved ICOTYDE (icotrokinra), an interleukin-23 (IL-23) receptor antagonist for the treatment of moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis.

key_facts.fact: In the ICONIC clinical program involving 2,500 patients across five Phase 3 studies, approximately 70% achieved clear or almost clear skin (IGA 0/1) at Week 16, and 55% achieved PASI 90 response (90%+ improvement). The safety profile was comparable to placebo within 1.1% difference.
key_facts.excerpt: ~70% achieved clear/almost clear skin (IGA 0/1) at Week 16. 55% achieved PASI 90 response (≥90% improvement) at Week 16. Safety profile comparable to placebo.

key_facts.fact: Head-to-head studies demonstrated superiority versus both deucravacitinib and ustekinumab. Until now, targeted biologics for psoriasis required injections; icotrokinra is taken as one tablet daily.
key_facts.excerpt: Head-to-head studies demonstrated superiority versus deucravacitinib and ustekinumab. ICOTYDE uniquely offers oral administration versus injectable biologics.

key_facts.fact: J&J EVP Jennifer Taubert called the approval 'a transformative shift in plaque psoriasis management.' Dr. John Reed (J&J R&D) said icotrokinra represents 'a fundamentally different treatment with potential to redefine patient expectations.'
key_facts.excerpt: Jennifer Taubert: 'marks a transformative shift in plaque psoriasis management.' Dr. John Reed: 'a fundamentally different treatment with potential to redefine patient expectations.'

sources.title: FDA approval of ICOTYDE (icotrokinra) ushers in new era for first-line systemic treatment of plaque psoriasis
